To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) year-specific and back-exploration of the 2008 LUR models for NO2 yield similar exposures at the national and regional scale for Great Britain; 2) year-specific models for 1990s have higher performance and lower bias in comparison with the back-exploration model for 2009; 3) back-exploration models are useful tools for estimating historic population air pollution exposure.
We developed year-specific LUR models for NO2 in Great Britain for the year 1991.
1991 NO2 LUR models developed for the UK using diffusion tube measurements and land use variables were more accurate than back-extrapolating a model from 2009.

developing robust methods for estimating historic air pollution exposure for health studies, and in particular, the effects of monitoring network bias on exposure estimation.
the development of robust methods to estimate historic air pollution exposures for epidemiological studies.
the development and validation of a new model for estimating long-term population exposures to nitrogen dioxide (NO2) in Great Britain.

the back-extrploation of the 2010 model is the most appropriate method for the 1990s.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of year-specific models for exposure assessment is feasible, and can yield better performance than back-extrapolations.
back-extrapolating LUR models can be used to assess historic population air pollution exposure, and that this approach yields similar exposure assessment to that from year-specific models.
